perHead.title: How the total breaks down by offence

notAvailable.note: NCRB doesn't publish a per-offence breakdown at city level for major metros. We won't show an estimate on a page people rely on - we'll add real figures here when they're available.

crime.illustrativeNote: Totals, rates and charge-sheeting are real NCRB data. The split across offence types below is an illustrative estimate - NCRB doesn’t publish a per-offence breakdown at city level for major metros.

heads.selectedTrend: Cases over time · total of selected heads · {y0}-{y1}
heads.compareHint: Hover or tap a bar to see both years' numbers.
heads.compareEmpty: No shared offence heads to compare for these two years. Try different years, or widen the scope filter.
heads.principalOffence: NCRB counts each case under one most-serious offence, so heads never double-count: the listed heads plus 'Other offences' add up to the city total. 'Other offences' is the real remainder of smaller heads NCRB lists, not missing data.
heads.naYear: NCRB publishes the per-offence split for {years}, not for {year}. Switch the year to {years} to see it.

crime.caveat: A rising line usually means more women are reporting - better access and trust - not necessarily more crime. The rate per lakh is the fairest way to compare cities to themselves over time.

headline.all: Reported crimes against women in Bengaluru have risen across most heads since 2018 - as much a sign of more reporting as of more crime.
headline.public: Across public-space heads, reported crime against women in Bengaluru has climbed since 2018 - cyber crime fastest of all.
headline.domestic: At home, cruelty by a husband or his relatives is by far the most-reported head - and most have risen since 2020.

justice.eyebrow: What happens after a case is filed
justice.title: Filing is only the start - here’s how cases move through the system, and why evidence and legal aid matter.
justice.convictionBody: Completed trials ending in conviction, Karnataka (2023). The rest end in acquittal - usually for want of evidence.
justice.pendingInvestigationBody: Cases still with police at year-end - before any trial begins.
justice.pendingTrialBody: 40,000+ cases awaiting trial - why timely evidence matters most.
justice.callout: These numbers describe the system, not you or your case. Strong evidence and a good lawyer are how cases beat these odds - so preserve evidence early and get legal aid.
justice.provisional: Disposal figures are state-level (Karnataka), provisional - source NCRB. City-level disposal to be added and marked separately.

footer.source: Source: NCRB “Crime in India” & Bengaluru City Police open data. Figures illustrative for concept; rates use principal-offence counts on a base of ~63 lakh women. No safety score, no city-vs-city comparison.

options.privacy: Nothing you enter here is saved or sent. It stays on your device.

step1.title: What happened?
step1.help: There’s no wrong answer, and you can change it anytime. Next we’ll ask roughly when, and whether you’re safe right now.

step2.title: Roughly when did this happen?
step2.help: The law changed on 1 July 2024. Knowing which side of that date this falls on lets us cite the correct rights - you can pick “not sure”.

step3.title: Are you safe right now?
step3.help: This doesn’t change your options below - it only decides whether to show immediate help first. You never have to answer.
step3.immediateHelp: If you’re in danger right now, call 112. You can also open a calm space to breathe.

step4.title: Today, do you want to act - or just understand?
step4.help: Both are completely valid. This only changes what we show first; every option stays available.

regimeNote.bns_bnss: Citations below are under the BNS/BNSS (in force since 1 July 2024).
regimeNote.ipc_crpc: This happened under the earlier IPC/CrPC. The rights are the same in substance, but the exact section numbers differ - we show the verified current-law reference and flag it rather than guess the old number.
regimeNote.unsure: We’re showing the current-law (BNS/BNSS) references. If your incident was before 1 July 2024, the rights are the same in substance but section numbers differ.

outcome.title: Here are your options. Every one of them is a valid next step.
outcome.lede: Take the one that feels right for you today. Nothing here commits you to anything.
outcome.lawCurrentNote: Current as of the BNS/BNSS (in force since 1 July 2024). Section references reviewed against the date shown.

context.rape: This is serious, and none of it is your fault. These paths fit best.
context.home: Because this is happening at home, these paths fit best.
context.dowry: Dowry demands are illegal. These paths fit best.
context.work: Because this happened at your workplace, these paths fit best.
context.stalking: Because you’re being followed or monitored, these paths fit best.
context.image_abuse: Because private images are involved, these paths fit best.
context.street: Because this happened in public, these paths fit best.
context.acid: This is grave, and you have strong rights. These paths fit best.
context.kidnapping: If someone is in danger right now, call 112. These paths fit best.
context.trafficking: You are the victim here, not the offender. These paths fit best.
context.pocso: A child’s safety comes first. These paths fit best.
context.unsure: It’s completely okay to just want to understand today.

outcome.reviewNote: This legal guidance is a first draft and is being reviewed by a qualified person before launch. It cites the current BNS/BNSS law; if your incident was before 1 July 2024 the rights are the same but section numbers differ.

grounding.title: You’re going to be okay.
grounding.body: There’s no rush, and nothing you have to decide right now. Take a few breaths. Stay here as long as you need - then choose what feels right.
grounding.bodyShort: There’s no rush and nothing you have to decide right now. Stay here as long as you need.

footer.storeNothing: We store nothing. This site is served as static files - there is no server that receives what you do here, no account, no tracking, no analytics on your choices.
